title: Priv IAM bootstrapper + least-privilege playbook for VPC deploys
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: deliver a reusable Terraform module (and playbook) that generates least-privilege IAM/RBAC artifacts for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments across AWS, GCP, and Azure. The module must: generate role/policy artifacts and bindings for service principals and human operator groups; support Kubernetes mappings (IRSA / Workload Identity) and SSO group->role mapping; provide safe upgrade paths and dual-binding canary rollout patterns; bundle a test harness (local and CI) for policy validation and runtime health checks; and emit clear outputs and example usage for operators.

Why this ticket: we have ad-hoc IAM templates across repos causing slow onboarding, risky broad privileges during upgrades, and no standardized health checks for policy drift. This module will be the canonical starting point used by Private customers and our on-prem packages.

Scope & deliverables:
- Terraform module: inputs for environment (account/project, region), primary service accounts, list of operator groups, and policy templates. Outputs: role_arns / role_ids, policy_document_ids, service_account_bindings, human_admin_temporary_role_arn.
- Multi-cloud support: canonical policies for AWS (IAM roles, managed policies, IAM conditions, resource boundaries), GCP (service accounts, IAM bindings), and Azure (managed identities, role assignments). Minimal surface for each cloud to avoid explosion of permutations.
- Least-privilege patterns: curated templates for common Redwood runtime roles (inference-runner, kv-cache-controller, metrics-exporter, console-readonly). Include progressive privilege escalation patterns (e.g., operator -> temp-admin with expiry, approve flow).
- Upgrade strategy: module versioning pragmatics, migration guide (renaming roles, replacing broad policy with scoped policies), zero-downtime dual-binding approach (create new role and attach, keep old role for 7 days, monitoring + rollback hooks).
- Canary rollout for IAM changes: automated plan to create new policy, attach to a small set of service accounts, run smoke tests, and expand. Provide a terraform/Makefile target to enact canary.
- Policy validation & CI: terraform validate, tflint, checkov, and conftest/OPA rules to assert no wildcard resources/verbs in production policies. Add a lightweight policy regression test suite that runs against LocalStack (AWS) or mocked APIs in CI to verify that typical calls succeed/fail as expected.
- Health checks: periodic drift detector (IAM Access Analyzer + custom scanning job), cloudtrail/event triggers for privilege spikes, daily synthetic tests that exercise least-privilege intents (e.g., metrics exporter can only push metrics), and an incident playbook for detected drift.
- Docs & examples: README with opinionated defaults, example overlays for a small customer using Dedicated GPUs, and a step-by-step upgrade playbook for operators. Link to RFC and design doc.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full RBAC UI in Console or SSO provisioning automation (those are follow-ups). It also doesn't attempt to model every 3rd-party integration (we'll provide extension points).

Acceptance criteria:
- Module released under registry/private-iam-bootstrapper v0.1.0 with CHANGELOG.
- CI pipeline enforces policy linting and runs the regression harness.
- Example overlay for AWS and GCP showing role creation, IRSA/Workload Identity mapping, and a canary policy change flow.
- Health check cronjob & alert playbook committed and verified in staging.
- Security review completed and sign-off recorded.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: accidental broad permissions during initial rollout. Mitigation: default policy templates are deny-by-default with explicit allow lists, CI blocks any commit that introduces wildcard CRUD permissions for prod label.
- Risk: cutover causing auth failures. Mitigation: dual-binding canary, automated smoke tests, and quick rollback script.
- Risk: cloud provider differences increase complexity. Mitigation: keep per-cloud primitives small, expose well-documented extension hooks for provider-specific needs.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype minimal module for AWS only (2 weeks) with example IRSA mapping and one runtime role.
2) Add policy validation tooling + CI integration (1 week).
3) Expand policies and templates, add GCP/Azure patterns (2 weeks).
4) Implement canary rollout targets and migration guide (1 week).
5) Add health checks + drift detector + docs + security review (1 week).

Links & artifacts:
- Design RFC: https://confluence.internal/redwood/priv-iam-bootstrapper-rfc
- Example overlays folder (draft): https://drive.internal/redwood/priv-iam-examples
- Draft PR for terraform module (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/962

Operational notes:
- Developers should be able to run make test-iam to execute the regression suite locally using LocalStack / emulator.
- Defaults should favor safety: ephemeral admin tokens expire after 1 hour by default and require explicit parameter to extend.
- Module should include an opt-in telemetry flag for admins to send anonymized policy-change events to our internal observability (off by default).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module v0.1.0 published with example overlays for AWS & GCP. 2) CI gates enforce tflint/checkov/conftest. 3) Canary rollout documented and exercised in staging. 4) Drift detection job deployed in staging with alerting to #priv-deploy-oncall. 5) Security review sign-off attached.
